Q: Apply multiple text filters at once and burn into video for captioning without re-encoding, and fix error [ffmpeg-python wrapper] A:

Short answer- No. By definition, adding text to the video requires changing the video itself. Re-encoding is required to perform this 'change' to the video.

Q: Data object structure for a daily reminder that may occur several times a day A:

Not really. Just store the duration and number of pills, and the next reminder time, and update it from the row data once you issue that reminder. Only one row required.

Q: Choosing between std::async vs IOCP for web server to handle multiple connections A:

You are really comparing apples and oranges, as they are vastly different APIs. Also, you didn't really provide any requirements, such as expected load and scaling. So, telling you which framework to use is not very practical. They can both accomplish your task. So can multiplexing non-blocking sockets without any multi-threading at all. So, just use whichever framework you are most comfortable with and meets your requirements.

Q: How can I count the number of open connections in an sqlite database? A:

According to these posts on the mailing list there is no way to check the number of open connections through code or the database itself. There is no API.

According to this post, if you are running on a POSIX type system you can use the lsof command to count how many processes have opened the database.

If you are on Windows you can use Process Explorer to count the number of connections with the following steps:

  1. In Process Explorer click on 'Find' -> Find Handle or DLL...
  2. Type in the name of your sqlite database and click on 'Search' (or hit Enter)
  3. In the results window, click on your database. It will become highlighted as a 'file' in the main Process Explorer window.
  4. Back in the main window, right-click on your database file and click Properties
  5. You can now see the number of References and Handles

Q: Is there a way to change the font color of the Release pipeline logs A:

Using ANSI Escape Codes (Custom Colors)

For more granular control, Azure Pipelines supports standard ANSI escape codes, which allow you to change text color without adding semantic icons like vso warnings or errors.

Color    Code
Red      \e[31m
Green    \e[32m
Yellow   \e[33m
Blue     \e[34m
Magenta  \e[35m
Cyan     \e[36m
Reset    \e[0m

Example Bash script:

bash

echo -e "\e[31mThis is red text\e[0m"
echo -e "\e[32mThis is green text\e[0m"

Example PowerShell script:

powershell

Write-Host "`e[33mThis is yellow text`e[0m"
Write-Host "`e[36mThis is cyan text`e[0m"

Q: Should I run VACUUM in transaction or after? A:

Vacuum is like defrag, it's good to do if you've recently deleted a lot of stuff, or maybe after you've inserted a lot of stuff, but by no means should you do it in every transaction. It's slower than almost any other database command and is more of a maintenance task.

We sometimes add/remove the majority of our db file, so then a vacuum would be a good idea, but I still would not consider it a part of the same transaction that did the work.

Q: Certificate signed by unknown authority error in Jenkins pipeline with Kubernetes cluster deployment A:

This is nicely explained inside Troubleshooting kubeadm TLS certificate errors

  • Verify that the $HOME/.kube/config file contains a valid certificate, and regenerate a certificate if necessary. The certificates in a kubeconfig file are base64 encoded. The base64 --decode command can be used to decode the certificate and openssl x509 -text -noout can be used for viewing the certificate information.
  • Unset the KUBECONFIG environment variable using:

unset KUBECONFIG

Or set it to the default KUBECONFIG location:

 export KUBECONFIG=/etc/kubernetes/admin.conf
  • Another workaround is to overwrite the existing kubeconfig for the “admin” user:

mv  $HOME/.kube $HOME/.kube.bak
mkdir $HOME/.kube
sudo cp -i /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf $HOME/.kube/config
sudo chown $(id -u):$(id -g) $HOME/.kube/config

Q: Getting StatusCode: 401, ReasonPhrase: 'Unauthorized', Version: 1.1, Content: System.Net.Http.StreamContent, Headers error when Calling a API via code A:

you must add the Authorization header, this one is added and calculated by postman, you can copy/post. the following if you are using a Basic authentication.

client.DefaultRequestHeaders.Authorization = new AuthenticationHeaderValue("Basic", "value to copy from postman");
